entertainment.body: BBC Studios has named Sreya Biswas the new head of its Natural History Unit (NHU). She takes over from Jonny Keeling, who is moving into a new role from early 2027, as previously unveiled. Reporting to Kate Ward , managing director, unscripted at BBC Studios , Biswas will work alongside creative directors Keeling and Mike Gunton, overseeing the unit’s teams based in Bristol. “Biswas will lead the editorial, commercial and strategic direction for the NHU as it sets an ambitious growth strategy for the future,” the company said. Biswas joined BBC Studios in the summer 2025 as the NHU’s Director of programs, where she oversaw a number of commissioned titles and the development of a portfolio of new content for multiple global clients across platforms, including the first BBC visualized nature podcast Naturewatch, feature documentary Matriarch , and Blue Planet III . Previously, she was served as head of commissioning for Natural History at the BBC, where she oversaw some of the landmark TV series, including Planet Earth III, Asia, Kingdom and Blue Planet III , as well as commissioning a broad range of natural history content, including Big Cats 24/7, Hamza’s Hidden Wild Isles, Spy in the Troop and A n Hour on Earth . Biswas also oversaw feature documentaries, such as Silverback and Orphan , as well as environmental thriller On Thin Ice: Putin v Greenpeace . “Sreya marries her extraordinary creative reputation and deep passion for the people and programmes of the NHU, with a razor-sharp future-facing vision that will look to deepen and strength how audiences can connect to the stories of the natural world,” said Ward. “We are delighted to welcome her to this pivotal role and look forward to continued success for the NHU under her inspiring leadership.” Said Biswas: “I feel hugely privileged to be stepping into this role, working alongside Mike Gunton and Jonny Keeling and leading the NHU’s remarkable teams. As the unit approaches its 70th year, we can look to the future with confidence and ambition, building on our unique reputation for innovation, integrity and unforgettable storytelling. entertainment.title: Russell Brand’s Ex-Girlfriend Accuses Him of “Violence, Coercive Control and Abuse”
entertainment.summary: TV producer Jemima Goldsmith took to social media after Brand received a 10-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault: "This was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact."
entertainment.body:
In the wake of his rape conviction, Russell Brand ‘s ex-girlfriend has accused him of “coercive control and abuse” while they were together.

The disgraced presenter and comedian was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday after being found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault by a London jury.

The court heard harrowing witness impact statements before the sentencing. One victim said: “I’ve been in shock and turmoil for weeks. I was extremely upset and traumatised. I didn’t have any respect for myself… I was thinking I was damaged goods — scared of giving off signals that could be taken the wrong way.” She continued that there were many times she felt “physically sick” seeing Brand in the media. “I just want to say, a leopard may change its spots, but it’s still a leopard.” Related Stories Movies 'Summer School, 2001,' the First Czech-Vietnamese Feature, Is Coming to America via Cinemas, Amazon (Exclusive) Movies Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama 'I Is Another' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM

The highly publicized trial and conviction have raised substantial questions across the industry over how Brand went unreported for so long. Just last week, a former associate of Brand’s accused of watching and laughing while the entertainer sexually assaulted a woman was asked to “step back” from his producing role. Jack Bayles, the head of comedy at independent TV production company Various Artists Limited (VAL), has worked on Michaela Coel’s I May Destroy You and Kat Sadler’s Such Brave Girls .

Now, TV producer Jemima Goldsmith, the ex-wife of former Pakistani prime minister and cricketer Imran Khan and the daughter of billionaire entrepreneur James Goldsmith, has taken to social media about her relationship with Brand. She said she was forced “to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident,” but did not end up pressing charges.

Goldsmith, who dated Brand for around a year in 2014, said the decision not to press charges or go public was down to her being worried about the impact of press attention on her then-teenage children. “I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014,” she wrote in a widely shared post on X. “Whilst my pain in relation to this pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact.”

entertainment.title: Nick Cannon Defends Feud With Eminem Over Mariah Carey: ‘You Can’t Come at My Wife’
entertainment.summary: The rapper dissed Carey and Cannon on his 2009 track "Bagpipes From Baghdad" after claiming he was in a relationship with the pop star
entertainment.body:
Nick Cannon reflected on his longtime feud with Eminem in a new interview. The conflict between Cannon and the Slim Shady rapper originated in 2009 when the rapper dissed Cannon’s ex-wife Mariah Carey and took aim at Cannon on “Bagpipes From Baghdad.”

“He disrespected my woman, man,” Cannon recounted during an appearance on On Par With Maury Povich . “You can’t come at my wife and don’t expect to get this work. I think he and Mariah had a professional relationship, which he professed to be a personal relationship.”

Cannon continued, “So that was way before me. So then by the time we got married, he had some harsh words because I guess he was still in his feelings. I couldn’t stand for that at the time. At the dignity of my woman, I had to fight for my relationship, my love.”

Cannon and Carey were married in 2008, although the beef between Carey and Eminem kicked off in the early ’00s. Eminem claimed that he was involved in a romantic relationship with the singer for a few months, which she has denied. He subsequently referenced her on several songs, including “When the Music Stops” and “Superman.” In 2002, Carey seemingly referenced the situation on her song “Clown,” singing, “You should’ve never intimated we were lovers/ When you know very well we never even touched each other.”

In 2006, Eminem reignited the feud on “Jimmy Crack Corn,” which included the lyrics “Your mind’s on us like mine’s on Mariah/ And y’all are just like her, you’re all fucking liars.” He then called out her and Cannon on “Bagpipes From Baghdad.” At the time, Cannon replied to the song in a since-deleted blog post, writing, “I thought we got past the days where white men could spew vulgar obscenities at our beautiful queens and get away with it.”

Cannon released a series of diss tracks taking aim at Eminem in December 2019, after he and Carey had divorced. These included “The Invitation,” “Pray for Him,” and “Canceled: Invitation.” The following year, he explained his intention in an interview with Billboard . “I was defending myself once again,” Cannon said. “He keeps bringing it up for decades. I’m one of those cats that matches energy. I don’t do it — I overdo it. Even in high school, I was a little guy, but if you made fun of me, I was gonna make fun of you, your momma, and that’s the same energy of Wild ‘N Out . It was a month of social commentary, but if you’ve ever heard me speak on this matter, I always give that dude his props as an icon in hip-hop. I think he knows better now. If he keeps talking about me, I’m gonna keep talking back.”

entertainment.title: Fall Out Boy Announce 2027 World Tour With The Offspring, Good Charlotte & More

entertainment.body:
Fall Out Boy have announced the Twilight of the Punks Tour on Monday (Nov. 9), a 36-date global run across stadiums and arenas in Europe, the U.K. and North America in 2027. They’ve also released “ACES,” their first new original single in more than three years, via Atlantic Records. Explore Fall Out Boy See latest videos, charts and news

The Live Nation-promoted tour opens May 17 at Prague’s O2 Arena and runs 15 dates through 11 European and U.K. countries, taking in Budapest, Milan, Madrid, Lyon, Brussels, Mönchengladbach, Glasgow, Dublin and Manchester. The leg peaks June 5 at London’s Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and wraps June 13 at Atlas Arena in Łódź, Poland. A Day to Remember and Neck Deep support throughout. Related Dr. Dre Says He's Going 'Off the Grid' for the First Time in His Career: 'I'm Going to Go Away' Tate McRae's 'Housewife' No. 1 on Global Charts for Third Week, Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' on the Prowl Cardi B, Travis Scott, Don Toliver & More to Perform at 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Festival

North America follows with 21 stadium dates, opening July 13 at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas, and closing Aug. 26 at Providence Park in Portland, Ore. The run includes Toronto’s Rogers Stadium, Boston’s Fenway Park, Citi Field in Queens, Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles and a hometown show at Chicago’s Soldier Field, the band’s first headline stadium date in the city where they formed. The Offspring and The Story So Far play all North American dates, with Good Charlotte on every show except Aug. 6 and 7.

“ACES” was produced and mixed by longtime collaborator Neal Avron, with a video directed by Brendan Walter. The release lands as the band marks 25 years together.

The rollout leaned on an elaborate online build. Fall Out Boy began teasing in late October with a post about a fictional “Twilight Town Mall,” then rebuilt their website as an interactive shopping directory. A “Two Quarters Arcade” followed, built with Brooklyn agency LOOP, letting fans remotely operate a real claw machine to win a band-branded plush. The band says it drew close to a million site visits and 6.1 million minutes of watch time, and crashed their servers.

Tickets go on general sale Thursday (Nov. 12) at 10 a.m. local time in North America and noon local in Europe and the U.K., with most markets excluding Lyon, Brussels, Paris and Łódź, which follow Friday (Nov. 13). An artist presale begins Wednesday (Nov. 11), alongside a Reserved by Spotify presale in select North American markets.

entertainment.title: Jimmy Kimmel Responds to Latest White House Attack: ‘Sick Burn, Bro’
entertainment.summary: The late-night host also speculated on how Donald Trump will spend his final two years in office
entertainment.body:
Donald Trump and the White House may still be recovering from the result of the election, but that hasn’t stopped them from taking aim at Jimmy Kimmel yet again. The late-night host responded to the latest barb from the White House on Monday night’s episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live .

“And then the White House got back to the important business of attacking me,” Kimmel explained of the election aftermath. “I got another statement from White House spokesperson Davis Ingle, who wrote, ‘Jimmy Kimmel’s case of Trump Derangement Syndrome is so advanced that it has completely rotted his peanut-sized brain. He’s far more entertaining when you’re laughing at him than with him. But unfortunately, his real talent is his failing ratings.'”

“Sick burn, bro,” Kimmel replied. “You know what? You should enter a rap battle spitting dope rhymes like that.”

He added, “Trump now has interns insulting me. It’s like that sad day when your cat gets to fat to chase mice. This guy says I have a peanut-sized brain. Let me explain something: I know you’re young. That’s impossible. You know what happens when you try to run a full human body with a peanut-sized brain?”

Kimmel then cut to a clip of Trump giving a speech where he pronounced “human genome” as “human g-nome.” “You start saying things like that guy,” Kimmel confirmed. “He has a brain like a p-nut.”

The host continued of Trump’s current demeanor, “I don’t think we’re prepared for the amount of insanity that this drama queen president is about to pump on us. Donald Trump right now is a raccoon in a duffel bag. He’s been cut off at the cankles. And there are two possible paths he can take. The first one is to check out. No more meetings. Lots of trips to Mar-a-Lago. Lots of golf with Natalie running behind the cart. Every once in a while he’ll host a Super Bowl team. That’s the best case scenario.”

entertainment.title: Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led to Her Social Media Break: “A Lot of Ugliness”
entertainment.summary: The actress plays the controversial Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO’s 'Game of Thrones' prequel series.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Olivia Cooke is getting candid about one of the reasons she took a break from social media, saying there’s “a lot of ugliness” in House of the Dragon fandom.

The actress, who plays controversial Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO’s Game of Thrones prequel series, recently chatted with GQ about the passionate yet intense fanbase that often theorizes about not only her character but sometimes herself and her relationship with directors.

“I think some of those interpretations just catch fire, and they become something that bears no resemblance to what was shown on the screen at the time,” Cooke said. “There’s a lot of ugliness to that fandom as well. It’s steeped in misogyny. There’s a lot of racism. I try to let it take up minimal mental real estate.” Related Stories Movies 'Summer School, 2001,' the First Czech-Vietnamese Feature, Is Coming to America via Cinemas, Amazon (Exclusive) Movies Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama 'I Is Another' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM

Eventually, the fan discourse on social media reached a point that was “not nourishing” for the actress, which is partly why she deactivated her social media accounts ahead of the House of the Dragon season three premiere in June.

“I was just like, I’m on this too much. It’s not nourishing,” she said. “I think the celebri-fied nature of being an actor has now snowballed into this monster. And I just think we need to get off this train and realise that we make these TV shows and films, yes, for escapism, but also because it’s artful and it’s creative and it’s not for followers or for a brand deal or to get free shit. Even though that is nice sometimes.”

Cooke isn’t the only actor in the Game of Thrones universe to open up about the negative impact of social media. Sophie Turner, who played Sansa Stark in the original series starting at the age of 14, told Flaunt last year that it started to take a toll on her mental health as a young actress.

“I think social media was just really becoming a big thing after I started on Game of Thrones , so I got a couple of years of peace and quiet and then I had to adjust. It had such a profound impact on my mental health, like more than I could tell you,” Turner said. “It almost destroyed me on numerous occasions.”

entertainment.title: Inside James Gunn, Peter Safran’s DC Ouster: Exec Tensions and a Fateful David Ellison Visit
entertainment.summary: The duo thought they were safe and were already plotting a third 'Superman' movie. Then, Skydance co-CEOs Ellison and Ynon Kreiz paid them a fateful visit on the Warner Bros. lot.
entertainment.body:
Logo text DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were feeling pretty secure under the new Skydance regime.

After surviving a merger that claimed the jobs of celebrated Warner Bros. heads Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy, the duo were basking in the modest success of Clayface , a horror movie released Oct. 21 that passed $100 million globally on a $44 million budget. There was even talk of doing more spooky, slimmed-down DC movies.

Gunn had also wrapped production on Man of Tomorrow , his sequel to Superman that is heading for a July 2027 release, and sources say he was in the midst of writing a third installment as part of plan to make a trilogy and release a Superman movie every two years, maybe even morphing the franchise into a Justice League teamup. Related Stories Midterms 2026 Six Hollywood Consequences of Tuesday's Democratic Blockbuster TV Chuck Lorre Talks David Ellison Optimism, Scientology and the Perks (Really!) of Working for Roseanne Barr

Then came Friday, Nov. 6, when Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz arrived at Gunn and Safran’s offices on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank. There, according to sources, the DC heads were told that despite previous assurances they would be part of the new Skydance mega-studio, Ellison and Kreiz had a change of plans. And now, after four years as two of the most visible faces in comic book films and TV, they were out .

And their replacement was surprising. It wasn’t a splashy C-suiter or an exec recently ousted amid Hollywood consolidation.

It was Jeremy Latcham, a mild-mannered producer who was once a key member of Marvel Studios’ exec team before moving to Texas to go independent.

An occasional foray into big-budget moviemaking such as Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves notwithstanding, Latcham was focusing on inspirational movies such as the Wright Brothers feature Flyer , for the faith-focused studio Wonder Project, where he also helped make House of David , a TV show about the Biblical figure. The producer is known to be vocal about his Christian faith and his desire to make uplifting projects.

“I had this nagging feeling that I needed to do more movies that had deeper meaning to me,” Latcham said of Wonder Project during an appearance on the Bible Bros podcast while promoting the Nate Bargatze comedy The Breadwinner . “Let’s be the HBO for the faith and family audience. Let’s try to make movies and television shows that restore faith in things worth believing in.”

entertainment.body:
Love him or loathe him, Johnny Depp is back. Paramount held a number of press screenings for the scandal-plagued A-lister’s big Hollywood comeback feature, Ebenezer , over the last few days and the first reactions are hitting social media.

Ebenezer held its world premiere at the Whitby Hotel in New York City on Nov. 1. The film had its London premiere in Leicester Square on Monday night. Full critics reviews for the film drop on Nov. 12, but Paramount allowed people who had attended the various screenings to post brief reactions to the film on social media. Ebenezer hits theaters globally on Nov. 13. Related Stories Movies Alan Ritchson Taps Alex Jackson to Serve as President at Dancing Skeleton Production Company Movies Helene Hahn Loyd, Former Disney and DreamWorks Exec, Dies at 78

The latest adaptation of Charles Dickens’ classic 1843 novella A Christmas Carol , Ebenezer is a more black comedy take on the trials and tribulations of one Ebenezer Scrooge. Set in Victorian London, the film follows Scrooge (Depp), a miserly businessman who has a particular hatred for Christmas. Scrooge goes on a redemption journey after being visited by three spirits.

The film has a stellar cast featuring the likes of Tramell Tillman , Ian McKellen , Rupert Grint , Andrea Riseborough , Sam Claflin , Daisy Ridley , Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber and Henry Lloyd-Hughes.

Ebenezer is directed by Ti West , the filmmaker behind A24’s highly regarded X trilogy as well as The Roost (2005), Trigger Man (2007), The House of the Devil (2009), The Innkeepers (2011) and In a Valley of Violence (2016). Nathaniel Halpern wrote the screenplay.

There is a lot riding on Ebenezer for Depp. The film is the Oscar-nominated actor’s first mainstream Hollywood feature since the fallout from his divorce from Amber Heard and subsequent legal battles. Once one of the entertainment industry’s most bankable stars, Depp has barely worked since 2020, starring in the 2023 French film Jeanne du Barry , and directing and producing (but not starring) in the Italy-produced biopic Modì, Three Days on the Wing of Madness in 2024.

After Ebenezer , Depp is set to star in Lionsgate’s supernatural thriller Day Drinker in 2027.

It was music to Millennials' ears when Carson Daly announced that the next two weeks of live shows will pay homage to Y2K, a time period responsible for producing some of the best songs of all time. Just hearing him say those words gave us warm-and-fuzzy flashbacks to the days of "TRL." Images of colorful iMac desktops, flip phones, and frosted tips danced in our heads — not that they ever really stopped.

Following a group performance of Backstreet Boys' "Everybody (Backstreet's Back")," we heard from the remaining members of Queen Latifah and Adam Levine's teams : Mia Knight, Dakota Cohen, Lillie Kolich, Connor Closs, BigCountry, and Lexi Stephens. The remaining artists from Kelly Clarkson and Riley Green's teams — including whichever singer was voted into the Top 13 last week — will perform live next Monday.

Read on for a breakdown of how this week's six artists performed, including which five are proceeding to the Top 10, and which one was eliminated from the competition.

Mia Knight kicked off the show's two-week salute to Y2K with "Miss Independent," one of the first (and most iconic) hits from Queen Latifah's fellow "Voice" coach Kelly Clarkson. Latifah encouraged the young singer to give her performance "all the sass and style" she could muster. We already knew that the 16-year-old has a voice beyond her years, but that maturity also showed itself in Knight's overall presentation on Monday; she approached the performance with confidence, owning every inch of the stage. Nerve did come into play on a few brief occasions, but Knight did not come to play, and it was strong overall, with some very big notes in there. The performance even got Clarkson's seal of approval, which is worth more than any votes. ( TVLine's grade: B+)

Adam Levine had us all looking to the skies with his pick for Dakota Cohen — Aerosmith's "I Don't Want To Miss A Thing," an unforgettable anthem written for the 1998 movie "Armageddon." And he wouldn't let her take it down a half-step either, insisting that she give the performance all that she's got. If possible, Cohen actually gave it even more than that. She slathered the song with all of the grit and growl that we've come to expect from her, along with several explosive moments that ultimately earned her a well-deserved standing ovation from the coaches. We're sure Steven Tyler would tip his hat to Cohen for this one... and then probably say something weird. ( TVLine's grade: A)

“Brand will be a marked man while he is there and — if he is to stay safe — needs to move quickly,” he said.

According to the outlet, Brand is currently being housed in his own cell due to concerns about his safety.

Actors talk about "the moment before," we always think about that before a scene, but the moment before the season, Bill's coming back and his father has died. That's quite a circumstance to thrust him back into work, and coming back for the first day of work after bereavement leave. So already there was just all this juicy circumstance to play with. And then, of course, he has this bomb dropped on him that his father had this secret life. I'm filming Episode 10 right now, and it's so satisfying. I was praising the writers just a few days ago at how great they did with throwing everything up in the air and then bringing a beautiful culmination by Episode 10.

But Episode 6, I'm really proud of. It took a lot out of me physically and emotionally, but that's because it's that point in the story where we're at. Bill is going to be led down his darkest path yet because of Felix Vincente, the assassin, and if audiences were wondering if the clean-cut, buttoned up, by the book FBI agent was gonna turn, this is it. These are certainly the circumstances.

entertainment.title: Nick Cannon Reflects on Eminem Feud After He Dissed Mariah Carey: ‘You Can’t Come at My Woman & Not Expect to Get This Work’
entertainment.summary: Cannon dropped a trio of diss tracks on Slim Shady in December 2019.
entertainment.body:
Nick Cannon joined the On Par With Maury Povich podcast on Monday (Nov. 9), where he reflected on his feud with Eminem, which was sparked by Slim Shady dissing Cannon’s ex-wife, Mariah Carey , in 2009.

“He disrespected my woman, man,” Cannon told former Maury host. “You can’t come at my wife and don’t expect to get this work. I think he and Mariah had a professional relationship, which he professed to be a personal relationship.”

Cannon continued: “So that was way before me. So then by the time we got married, he had some harsh words because I guess he was still in his feelings. I couldn’t stand for that at the time. At the dignity of my woman, I had to fight for my relationship, my love.”

Cannon and Carey tied the knot in 2008. Em implied that he previously was romantically involved with the pop star on 2009’s “Bagpipes From Baghdad.” The Wild ‘N Out creator addressed Em in a since- deleted Tumblr post.

Many believe Carey’s response came with her “Obsessed” single later that year, which saw her play a man resembling Slim Shady in the top 10 Billboard Hot 100 hit’s visual. Em appeared to reply to Carey and Cannon on “The Warning” in July 2009.

Carey and Cannon’s divorce was finalized in November 2016 and all was quiet on the feud front with Eminem — that is, until the Drumline star’s appearance on T.I.’s Expeditiously podcast, which revived the beef with the Detroit rapper. Eminem seemingly jabbed at Cannon with his verse on Fat Joe’s “Lord Above.”

Cannon proceeded to unleash a trifecta of diss tracks taking aim at Eminem in December 2019: “The Invitation,” “Pray for Him” and “Canceled: Invitation,” the latter of which attempted to paint Em as a racist with old remarks.

Eminem didn’t dip his pen to respond on wax or in the studio, but only with a short reply on X as their feud heated up.

entertainment.title: Steve Buscemi Reveals Which Show He Refuses to Appear on: “I Don’t Care How Much You Paid Me”
entertainment.summary: Here's a hint: the 'Wild Horse Nine' actor doesn't do spicy food.
entertainment.body:
If you were hoping to see Steve Buscemi take on the hot wings challenge, don’t bet on it.

During a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , host Josh Horowitz asked the veteran actor, who’s promoting his new films Wild Horse Nine and Klara and the Sun , about things he dislikes.

“I’m confused why people like spicy food, why they like their mouths hot,” Buscemi replied. So First We Feast’s Hot Ones , hosted by Sean Evans , likely won’t ever be a stop on the actor’s press tours. Related Stories Movies 'Klara and the Sun' Review: Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams Should Have Insisted on a Factory Reset for Taika Waititi's Cloying, Clumsy AI Fable Movies John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell Buddy Up for London Film Festival Premiere of 'Wild Horse Nine'

“Sam Rockwell told me that he and Parker Posey did Hot Ones — that’s something I would never do. I don’t care how much you paid me, how much they said, ‘But it would really support the film,’ no. It not only makes me confused, it makes me angry,” he added with a laugh. “You’ll never get me, Hot Ones !”

In recent years, Hot Ones , which launched in 2015, has become a routine stop for celebrities as they’re making the rounds to promote their latest projects. The YouTube talk show, created by Evans and Christopher Schonberger, sees the host interviewing guests as they eat a platter of ten wings, each coated in a progressively hotter hot sauce.

Dozens of celebrities have taken on the challenge, including Jennifer Lawrence, Paul Rudd, Billie Eilish, Post Malone, Conan O’Brien, Charlize Theron, Pedro Pascal and Shaquille O’Neal, among others. But seeing many stars end in tears or yell in pain (“I feel like I’m gonna die,” Lawrence said during her episode) likely wasn’t a selling point for Buscemi.

Earlier this year, Evans revealed some of his favorite Hot Ones episodes during a chat with Matt Belloni. “I always say if you’re new to the show, check out the Conan O’Brien episode or the Gordon Ramsay episode. Jennifer Lawrence is another one or Maya Rudolph. Paul Rudd is a classic. Charlize Theron,” he said at the time. “I always say to start with those. If you like those episodes, you’ll probably like the show. If you don’t like those episodes, stop there. There’s nothing for you.”

Spanish-Mexican singer Alaska, Cuban-Mexican musician Francisco Céspedes, Mexican singer-songwriter Lila Downs , Brazilian artist Daniela Mercury and Dominican singer-songwriter Chichí Peralta received Lifetime Achievement Awards for their creative contributions of outstanding artistic value to Latin music. entertainment.body:
Billy Joel surprisingly made an announcement that he’s putting on a show despite doctors telling him he can no longer perform or even drive anymore.

The legendary musician, 77, shared on Instagram Monday that he’ll be performing at Florida Atlantic University on Dec. 14 for an event titled “Billy Joel for Billy Joel: An Evening of Questions & Answers…And a Little Music.”

Tickets for the intimate event, which is set to feature a Q&A segment and some live music, will only be available to currently enrolled Florida Atlantic University students.

The performance will mark his first appearance since he revealed in September that he had brain surgery after he was diagnosed with normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in 2025. NPH is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid builds up inside the skull and presses on the brain and disrupts brain function, per the Cleveland Clinic

Joel told the Hollywood Reporter last month that while he wanted to continue to perform, doctors advised him against it.

“I have to take a series of tests before I know,” he told the outlet.

He explained that his doctors were concerned about the combination of extreme sound volume, lighting, stress and energy while he’s on stage.

“What the neurologist told me, every time you do a show, it’s like you’re getting a concussion,” he shared.

sports.title: Greg Rousseau: Bills defense showing "what we can do" over last two weeks
sports.summary: The Bills gave up at least 29 points in five of their first six games of the season and opponents averaged over 386 yards of offense in those contests.
sports.body:
Concern about those numbers was mitigated by the team’s 5-1 record, but it lingered as a reason to doubt that the Bills would be able to go the distance come the postseason. The Bills had a bye in Week 7 and the last two weeks have seen very different performances.

The Bills allowed 144 yards in a 36-10 win over the Ravens in Week 8 and they allowed 178 in Monday night’s 23-6 win over the Vikings. They recorded six sacks and six takeaways in those games and the defensive effort on Monday bought their offense time to get going after a poor start to the game.

Linebacker Greg Rousseau had a sack in each win to get to eight for the season and he said the performances show a unit that is discovering its identity.

“Last week wasn’t a fluke ,” Rousseau said, via Lance Lysowski of the Buffalo News . “It’s what we are. It’s what we can do. We just have to keep going.”

The counter to Rousseau or anyone else feeling bullish about the Bills defense is that Joe Fagnano was at quarterback for most of the Ravens game and that Carson Wentz was running the Vikings offense. The Bills can’t control such things, of course, but they do make it harder to feel like the results were all about tweaks that had improved the defense.

General Manager Brandon Beane has a chance to bolster the group before Tuesday afternoon’s deadline and games against the Jets and Dolphins offer chances to keep building confidence over the next two weeks. Those things could help because the real tests of the Bills defense won’t come for some time.

sports.title: Carson Wentz: This one felt pretty terrible
sports.summary: The Vikings' quarterback had perhaps the worst game any NFL quarterback has had this season in Monday night's loss to the Bills.
sports.body:
“This one felt pretty terrible. I’m not going to lie,” Wentz said, via the Associated Press.

Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards, with no touchdowns and two interceptions against the Bills. His passer rating of 8.9 was the lowest for any quarterback in any game in which he threw more than three passes this season. Wentz said he knows the Vikings’ defense can win with competent quarterback play, and he did not provide that.

“To go kind of lay an egg, personally, the way I struggled early, especially with our defense playing as good as they’ve been all year, honestly,” Wentz said. “They did it again tonight, and we just didn’t help them out. I didn’t help them out. It’s hard to put my finger on the why.”

The Vikings need to put their finger on the how, as in how to fix their offense. Or else a great defense is going to waste.

sports.title: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez had a game so bad, he did something never seen before
sports.summary: When Christian Gonzalez signed a four-year, $135 million contract with the Patriots before the season, it was a new record for a cornerback.
sports.body:
According to Next Gen Stats , which uses player tracking to determine which defensive back is in coverage on every pass thrown in every game, Gonzalez had a bad game against two Packers receivers that was unlike anything seen before.

Gonzalez allowed seven catches for 105 yards to Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden, and three catches for 82 yards to Packers wide receiver Christian Watson. Gonzalez is the only defender, as far back as Next Gen Stats go (since at least 2018) to allow more than 80 receiving yards in coverage to two different players in the same game.

Head coach Mike Vrabel said the Patriots expect better from Gonzalez , and he expects better from himself. The Patriots need to be better on Sunday, when they’re playing a Lions offense that also focuses its passing game around two big-play wide receivers, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. They must be licking their chops watching film of Gonzalez this week.

sports.title: James Cook's 31 carries vs. Vikings were the most in any NFL game this season
sports.summary: Against a Vikings defense that has been teeing off on opposing quarterbacks this season, Bills coach Joe Brady knew he needed to lean on his running back on Monday night.
sports.body:
And so he did, with Bills running back James Cook getting 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 23-6 win over the Vikings.

Cook’s 31 carries were the most any running back has had in any NFL game this season.

Cook led the NFL with 1,621 rushing yards last season, but he’s actually been even more productive so far this season. He’s averaging both more carries per game and more yards per game in 2026 than he did in 2025. Josh Allen makes the Bills’ offense go, but the Bills rely on their running back as much as any team in the NFL, and on Monday night, Cook delivered.

sports.title: Justin Jefferson: Vikings' offense didn't get it done, we've got to figure it out
sports.summary: Jefferson finished with three catches for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills.
sports.body:
“The offense didn’t get it done,” Jefferson said. “Defense did a phenomenal job once again, getting it done against a very good offense. We’ve got to figure it out on offense.”

Jefferson said everyone on the offense has to do better, although he admitted he doesn’t know all the answers.

“We’ve got to figure it out,” Jefferson said. “That’s something we don’t have the answer to at the moment. We’ve just got to figure it out.”

Although quarterback Carson Wentz was terrible on Monday night, and Kyler Murray hasn’t been much better for most of the season, Jefferson called it “an all 11 thing” and said it’s not just on the quarterback.

“It doesn’t really matter who’s throwing the ball, as long as it gets to us, that’s all that matters, and it’s up to us to make those plays. It’s tough. Definitely tough,” Jefferson said.

sports.title: Kevin O'Connell on potential quarterback trade: "I'll defer to Nolan [Teasley] on that"
sports.summary: Vikings coach doesn't rule out making a deal by Tuesday's deadline.
sports.body:
“I’ll defer to [G.M.] Nolan [Teasley] on that,” O’Connell said. “We’ve had dialogue about a lot of different positions. And tight turnaround obviously playing the Monday night game before that, and we’ll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape, or form.”

O’Connell was asked at one point whether he has ever felt as challenging as it does right now, as a play-caller.

They have options. Several teams could be looking to make a deal. And even if it won’t be cheap, it’s necessary to salvage what was, only nine days ago, a very promising season.

It still can be. A return of Kirk Cousins would be a B-12 shot to the franchise. Even Daniel Jones would make things better than they are.

And if they want to go all in, try to make a deal for Justin Herbert — who may be thrilled at this point to don an eye patch and escape from L.A.

Whatever the Vikings do, they need to do something. Otherwise, there may not be a quarterback change when the season ends.

sports.title: Receiver-needy teams should call about Justin Jefferson
sports.summary: If the Vikings aren't going to upgrade at QB, they should give Jefferson a chance at a championship.
sports.body:
Few players are untouchable, when it comes to a trade. And even if the Vikings would hang up the phone and not listen, teams that need a high-end pass-catcher should try.

The Rams currently are in a pickle, thanks to the placement of Puka Nacua on injured reserve, where he joins Davante Adams. The Chiefs could use help at the position, too.

Ditto for the Steelers, who (like the Chiefs and Commanders) have interest in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

Then there are the 49ers, who are always lurking when it comes to possibly making a big move.

Regardless, it makes sense to make the call. If the Vikings aren’t going to make a move for a functional quarterback, they should stockpile picks and give Jefferson a chance to chase the championship that won’t happen in Minnesota — especially if they waste his seventh season by not upgrading at the quarterback position.

Yes, a trade would come with a 2027 cap charge. The Vikings also would avoid the $30 million he’s due to make in 2027, and the upgrade to meet the increased market that he surely already wants.

At the end of the day, it’s one or the other. Trade for a better quarterback, or trade Jefferson to another team. Of the available options, doing neither makes the least sense.

sports.title: James Cook powers through against Vikings for important Bills win
sports.summary: ESPN named James Cook the player of the game in their postgame show and it’s easy to see why. The Buffalo Bills leaned on their running back against the Minnesota Vikings, and despite a slow start, Cook delivered over the course of the game and scored what felt like the game-ending touchdown with 6:
sports.body: ESPN named James Cook the player of the game in their postgame show and it’s easy to see why. The Buffalo Bills leaned on their running back against the Minnesota Vikings, and despite a slow start, Cook delivered over the course of the game and scored what felt like the game-ending touchdown with 6:17 left in the fourth quarter. That’s seven straight games with a rushing touchdown for Cook. He also has 75+ rushing yards in those games, the longest streak in team history with 75 yards and a touchdown run. That combo is the longest streak by a player since 2006 when LaDanian Tomlinson had eight straight. Cook’s previous career high in carries came in 2025 when he ran the ball 32 times with two offensive lineman injured against a really talented Pittsburgh Steelers defense. The same thing happened in Minnesota, when two Bills offensive linemen were on the shelf and Buffalo needed the help. Cook toted the rock 31 times for 107 yards at a tough 3.5 yards per carry. Cook’s long was only 11 yards on Monday. In the passing game, Cook was targeted once but let the Allen pass go through his hands but he probably wouldn’t have picked up many yards anyway. The rest of the rushing game was shaky at best. Josh Allen ran the ball five times for 16 yards (outside the first half kneel down), mostly on designed runs. Ray Davis had two runs for two yards. Ty Johnson had one rush for one yard. There was some consternation about signing Cook to his current contract a while ago, but that seems to have passed. Cook deserves a ton of credit for continuing to grind against the Vikings. It’s a short week for the Blls heading into a Sunday game after a road trip on Monday night, so hopefully he can get iced up with a veteran rest day this week. After the game, Cook was nonchalant on how his body feels. “[I feel] excellent. Feel like I didn’t play a game.” Hopefully he feels that way in the morning.

sports.title: Bills bludgeon Vikings 23-6, stay atop the AFC
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills now sit at 7-1 after defeating the Minnesota Vikings 23-6. Allen and Cook made NFL history by reaching 5,000 rushing yards as teammates.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: Bills wear down Vikings, 23-6
sports.summary: The Bills had 79 plays and held the ball for 42:32.
sports.body:
The Bills wore down the Vikings, winning 23-6 to move to 7-1. The Vikings lost their second consecutive, falling to 6-2. They have not scored more than 16 points in their past three games.

The Vikings were downright inept on offense Monday night, gaining 178 yards on 46 plays, with nine first downs, three turnovers and five punts. They were 0-for-8 on third down and 0-for-2 on fourth down.

Carson Wentz was no better than Kyler Murray, and in fact, had one of the worst quarters a quarterback has ever had in the third quarter. Wentz went 0-for-4 with two interceptions in the third quarter and should have had a third pick on a pass that Terrel Bernard dropped after it hit him between the numbers.

Wentz finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards with two interceptions. Justin Jefferson caught three of 11 targets for 58 yards and was visibly frustrated.

The Vikings’ field-goal drives covered 9 and 46 yards, with Will Reichard hitting from 43 and 53 for the team’s only points.

Max Brosmer may have won the job by going 6-of-7 for 58 yards before the Vikings turned it over on downs at the Buffalo 13 on their final drive.

The Bills gained 399 yards on 79 plays, wearing down the Vikings’ defense by possessing the ball for 42:32. James Cook ran for 107 yards and a touchdown on 31 carries; Josh Allen was 21-of-31 for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception; and eight players caught at least one pass, including tight end Keleki Latu, whose first career touchdown covered 25 yards.

Tyler Bass was perfect again, making kicks from 39, 25 and 52 yards and running his streak to 24 in a row.

sports.title: The Vikings need to trade for a quarterback tomorrow
sports.summary: Failure to act leads to one conclusion: The Vikings are dysfunctional.
sports.body:
What will they do about a team with a Super Bowl-caliber defense and an offense that could barely function in the MAC?

The window remains open until 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The Vikings were in this spot three years ago, when Kirk Cousins tore an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline.

That time, the Vikings didn’t have many options; they ended up with Josh Dobbs. This time, there are two former Vikings on other teams who know the Minnesota offense: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins.

If the calls haven’t already been made, they should be. Immediately. What will it take to salvage a season that is disintegrating before everyone’s eyes, despite the 6-2 record?

It wouldn’t be easy to plug and play a new quarterback, but there’s history with Jones and Cousins. It would be easier to get them up to speed than if they brought in someone who would be learning everything from scratch.

If, in the end, the Colts want too much for Jones and the Raiders want too much for Cousins (neither is untouchable; the question is the amount of the compensation), the only other starter potentially available would be Geno Smith.

Some have suggested a play for Justin Herbert. At this point, however, it’s impossible to know whether his implosion is about his surroundings or about Herbert.

Then there’s Jimmy Garoppolo, who remains a free agent — and who has been largely forgotten.

sports.title: Josh Allen becomes fifth NFL quarterback with 5,000 rushing yards
sports.summary: Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards in the NFL. For a guy whose primary job is throwing the football, that’s a lot of ground covered. The Buffalo Bills quarterback became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach that total during Buffalo’s Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Allen cr
sports.body: Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards in the NFL. For a guy whose primary job is throwing the football, that’s a lot of ground covered. The Buffalo Bills quarterback became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach that total during Buffalo’s Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Allen crossed the 5k mark in the third quarter on a series of designed runs. He entered the game at 4991 then had a 7-yard run in the first quarter to get to 4998. He lost one yard on the kneel down to end the first half to fall back to 4997. A 5-yard scramble from the Minnesota 21 was followed by a 3-yard run to make sure he was over. And counting… Allen joins Lamar Jackson, Michael Vick, Cam Newton, and Russell Wilson in the 5,000-yard group. That’s the entire list, and Allen has put himself on it in his ninth NFL season. Bills fans have watched those yards come a few different ways. There have been scrambles after the protection breaks down, designed runs, and more than a few plays where Allen decides the best way to get a first down is to go through whoever is standing in front of him. They all count. Of course, if he slid more often, like we all keep screaming for him to do, it would have taken a few more carries to get there. Allen already owns the NFL record for career rushing touchdowns by a quarterback. Now he has another number to go with it, and another reminder of how much of Buffalo’s offense has come from his legs.

sports.title: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson will miss multiple weeks with a knee issue

The Patriots were already down their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, top two guards Michael Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker, and backup running back TreVeyon Henderson.

Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are the only healthy running backs on the 53-player roster but signed Terrell Jennings to the practice squad last week.

sports.title: Josh Allen ties Peyton Manning for NFL touchdown record
sports.summary: Josh Allen has done it again. He has rewritten another NFL record. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has tied Peyton Manning for the most combined touchdowns by a quarterback in his first 10 NFL seasons. Yes, you read that right. His first 10 seasons. Allen is only in Year 9. With his first touchdown pa
sports.body: Josh Allen has done it again. He has rewritten another NFL record. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has tied Peyton Manning for the most combined touchdowns by a quarterback in his first 10 NFL seasons. Yes, you read that right. His first 10 seasons. Allen is only in Year 9. With his first touchdown pass against the Minnesota Vikings, Allen brought his career total to 322, moving even to the 322 touchdowns Manning recorded during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2119984341048537488] Of course, Allen has had a little help from his legs along the way. Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, while Allen has been putting up numbers as both a passer and a runner since Buffalo drafted him in 2018. But here’s where the numbers get interesting. Manning played 160 regular-season games during his first 10 seasons. Allen entered Week 9 of the 2026 season with just 135 games under his belt and tied Manning in his 136th game. That’s 24 fewer games, and Allen still has the rest of this season and all of 2027 to add to his total. Allen also moves ahead of some pretty familiar names on the all-time list, including Russell Wilson, Dan Marino, Brett Favre, and Cam Newton. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback who can still add to his first-10-season total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is in his 10th season and finished Week 9 with 301 touchdowns. He would need 21 more just to get past Manning’s mark, and with Allen still adding to his own total, that target is only going to get harder to reach. Dak Prescott and Jared Goff are also in the top 10, but both are already in their 11th _________________________________ Most combined touchdowns by a quarterback in their first 10 NFL seasons - Peyton Manning — 322 - Josh Allen — 322 - Russell Wilson — 316 - Patrick Mahomes — 301 - Dan Marino — 296 - Dak Prescott — 275 - Jared Goff — 269 - Brett Favre — 266 - Matt Ryan — 265 - Cam Newton — 261 Regular-season passing, rushing, and receiving touchdowns combined. ____________________________________ And with the rest of this season and all of 2027 still to play, Allen has plenty of time to add to that record before the final top number is set.

sports.title: Jaguars may plan for Jordan Davis to play more than 52 percent of the time
sports.summary: The good news for defensive tackle Jordan Davis is that he's been traded to a team in a state with no income tax.
sports.body:
In nine starts this season, Davis has been on the field for 52 percent of the defensive plays. Given what the Jaguars have given up to get him (next year’s first-round pick and a second-round selection in 2029), Jacksonville may be planning to increase his workload.

Unless the Jaguars make him a three-down player, it will be a massive investment for a run-stopping defensive tackle. And it explains the Eagles’ position that the Jaguars made an offer that Philly couldn’t refuse .

So either the Jaguars gave up too much, or Davis is going to be playing a lot more. There really isn’t a middle ground.

Regardless, the Jaguars are going for it. And it will be harder for them to fly under the Super Bowl radar after the trio of trades they made on Monday.

sports.title: Sam Darnold could return after the Seahawks' bye week
sports.summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will not play in Sunday's game against the Raiders, but he could return after the team's bye week.
sports.body:
Coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock is expected to start in Darnold’s stead despite oblique and throwing elbow injuries.

Darnold will miss a second consecutive game with quad and rib injuries, but he could be back for the showdown with the rival 49ers on Nov. 29.

“ I think so , yeah,” Macdonald told reporters Monday, via Cameron Van Til of Seattle Sports. “He’s making progress. We’re going to need some more time.”

The Seahawks also won’t have left guard Quenton Nelson, who will miss Sunday’s game with a knee injury. Macdonald said it’s “possible” that Nelson can return after the bye, too.

Nelson will undergo a “minor” knee procedure, per Macdonald.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: Bills lead Vikings 10-6 at halftime
sports.summary: Josh Allen threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds left in the first half for the halftime lead.
sports.body:
The Vikings are struggling to gain yards and score points Monday night against the Bills, who are struggling almost as much against the Minnesota defense.

The Vikings’ first four drives went three plays or less. Their first field goal — a 43-yard kick by Will Reichard — came on a four-play, 9-yard drive after a Bills’ punt out of their own end zone. Reichard added a 53-yarder with 5 seconds left in the half, completing a seven-play, 46-yard drive.

Two replay decisions went the Bills’ way in the first half: 1. Carson Wentz threw a lateral to Justin Jefferson that hit the ground and was covered by Bills defensive lineman Greg Rousseau at the Minnesota 44. Joe Brady challenged the on-field ruling of an incompletion, and replay reversed it to a fumble. The Bills got a 39-yard Tyler Bass field goal out of it. 2. Josh Allen was sacked by Andrew Van Ginkel at the Buffalo 2 and fumbled. Replay, though, showed Allen’s knee was on the ground before Van Ginkel knocked the ball loose.

The Bills outgained the Vikings 143 to 86 despite three sacks of Allen, who is 13-of-20 for 122 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

He threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds left in the first half after rolling to his right to buy time. It was Latu’s first career touchdown.

Allen was 6-for-6 on the eight-play, 80-yard touchdown drive.

Wentz is 7-of-17 for 75 yards, with Jefferson catching two for 39. Aaron Jones has three rushes for 10 yards.

sports.title: Tony Romo makes appearance on the Pat McAfee alt cast
sports.summary: Tony Romo has made a return to sports media.
sports.body:
Romo appeared remotely on the Pat McAfee alt cast during Monday night’s Bills-Vikings game. It’s the first Romo sighting on any platform since his August arrest for DUI and ensuing separation from CBS.

It’s the second McAfee alt cast of the season. The first one averaged 351,000 viewers on ESPN2, less than the Next Gen Stats alt cast on NFL Network, which attracted 469,000 viewers.

Romo’s next move will be interesting. He’s currently a free agent. Depending on the terms of his settlement with CBS, an offset obligation could apply as to anything he earns.

Regardless, Romo has resurfaced. Where it goes from here remains to be seen.

sports.title: Jake Ferguson, Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks for Cowboys
sports.summary: The Cowboys will play "multiple weeks" without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and backup running back Tyler Goodson, coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday.
sports.body:
Ferguson sprained the posterior cruciate and the medial collateral ligaments in his left knee in the third quarter Sunday, and Goodson injured his knee in the second quarter but played through it into the second half.

Goodson had a career-high 77 yards on 12 carries against the Colts.

“A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline, and this is a guy that has been incredible for us really the last two weeks,” Schottenheimer said, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “And these guys, they want to tough it out. They care. They want to win. They want to do whatever it takes. And just doing some more exams and scans and things like that, a few things showed up that we’ll keep an eye [out] for.”

The Cowboys have only one slot remaining on the injured reserve designated-to-return list, having already designated seven players.

Tight end Luke Schoonmaker has missed the past two games with a groin injury but will return this week, Schottenheimer said.

Fullback Hunter Luepke is the only player behind starting running back Javonte Williams on the active roster. Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin are on the practice squad.

“There’s a lot of different ways to do it,” Schottenheimer said of the running back situation. “I have a lot of confidence in Izzy. We’ll be looking at a lot of different potential moves that we can make, but I’m not going to pretend that losing Goody doesn’t affect us. The guy’s been playing great football.”

sports.title: Imaging showed no fracture in Justin Herbert's finger
sports.summary: Herbert injured his left middle finger on the final of eight sacks he took Sunday.
sports.body:
“So he should be good to go ,” Harbaugh said Monday, via the Associated Press.

Herbert injured his non-throwing hand on a sack by Logan Hall when the quarterback tried to stiff-arm the defensive lineman with 14:12 remaining in the fourth quarter. Herbert, who was sacked eight times in the 44-22 loss, threw a touchdown pass two plays later.

Herbert had his left hand surgically repaired during the 2025 season after breaking a bone in the back of the hand during a Week 13 game. He played through the injury and expects to play through his current injury, he said postgame.

sports.title: Klint Kubiak gives defensive coordinator Rob Leonard a vote of confidence
sports.summary: The Raiders defense allowed 38 points in the loss to the 49ers on Sunday, the sixth consecutive game of giving up 30-plus points.
sports.body:
“In fact, I see us doing the things we said we’re going to do [but] better,” Kubiak said, via Ryan McFadden of ESPN. “Stand behind, Rob. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players. And I think the world wants someone’s head on the platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason: to get a job done and develop players for the long haul.”

The Raiders ranked eighth in points allowed (18 ppg) and 11th in yards (316.8 ypg) in the team’s 3-0 start. Since Week 4, Las Vegas is last in points allowed (35.7 ppg), rushing yards allowed (168.7) and defensive efficiency (17.54) and 29th in sacks (nine).

“I have seen it work. Just not for four quarters,” Kubiak said of his defense. “As a group, it’s putting four quarters of football together no matter who’s the opponent. You play a damn good offense in San Francisco; there’s got to be a happy medium somewhere between the first half and second half.”

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills are holed up in cozy U.S. Bank Stadium and ready for a primetime showdown with the Minnesota Vikings under the spectacle that is Monday Night Football. Tonight, it’s a showdown between two 6-1 teams with vastly different roads to success in 2026. The Bills and their league-best scoring offense are of course led by quarterback Josh Allen while featuring one of the most lethal rushing attacks directed by running back James Cook III. Where they’ve struggled is on defense, and against opponents’ passing attacks. Is that a recipe for disaster this evening with wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison set to play catch with quarterback Carson Wentz? Well, expect Jefferson and Addison to get plenty of chances to see how they fare against cornerbacks Christian Benford and rookie Davison Igbinosun. Tonight does present a massive challenge for Buffalo’s offense. Allen will have an entirely new pair of offensive linemen protecting him on the left side — and against a ferocious Vikings pass rush. It’s not an ideal situation, to be clear, having a starting pair in left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson sidelined for this game. In their place will be offensive tackle Tylan Grable, and offensive guard Austin Corbett. No pressure, right? It’s time to find out what the next men up have up their sleeve to take on the NFL’s best and stingiest defense, a Vikings unit that blitzes as though their life depended upon it. It’s likely we see head coach Joe Brady call a lot of early runs and quick passes to both wear the defense down and allow Allen to settle into rhythm. Winning in the NFL is tough, and this might be the Bills’ biggest challenge yet. Though you may be looking for Allen and company to air it out, and expect Buffalo’s defense to continue an upward trajectory based off last week’s thrashing of the Baltimore Ravens, a win is a win, signature or otherwise. Remember, for those of you without cable or streaming service options, the ESPN broadcast is also shown live on your local ABC station. With that, here’s your open thread for all of tonight’s action during Bills at Vikings for Week 9 of Monday Night Football! As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua injury: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't questioning that play call
sports.summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders.
sports.body:
Nacua’s injuries occurred on the Rams’ final offensive play when he was tackled after rushing for five yards on third-and-11. Nacua took a handoff on the play and head coach Sean McVay was asked at a Monday press conference if he second-guessed himself for putting Nacua in position to take a hit at that point in the game.

McVay said he’s “kicking myself about those kinds of things” and called it something the Rams have to think about “internally” as they move forward.

“I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion, and maybe ended the game that would’ve led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee,” McVay said. “It’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we’ve got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine. He’s a guy we have to be intentional about because it’s a bummer. Because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don’t take that for granted.”

With Nacua and Davante Adams now out for the indefinite future, the Rams may be in the market for receiving help before the trade deadline passes at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They do not have their 2027 first- or third-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick or their 2029 third-round pick thanks to their trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.

sports.title: Eagles trade DT Jordan Davis to Jaguars
sports.summary: The Jaguars have gone all-in, and (as to 2027) the Eagles have checked out.
sports.body:
Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, the Eagles have traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars. In return, the Eagles will acquire a first-round pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2029.

It’s the second trade the Jaguars have made today for a defensive starter. The day began with the Jaguars sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons for safety Jessie Bates III, continued with a deal to acquire defensive tackle Davon Gochaux from the Saints for a 2028 sixth-round pick, and culminated in the blockbuster deal for Davis.

Unlike Bates, who is in the last year of his contract, Davis signed a new deal in March, a three-year, $78 million extension. The Eagles paid an $18.79 million signing bonus and half of Davis’s $1.215 million base salary.

The move will trigger a $15.428 million cap charge for the Eagles in 2027.

While the trade complicates further trades of significant veteran contracts, the willingness to deal Davis underscores the fact that most players are available for the right price, and that few are untouchable.

As to Davis, the Eagles happily converted the player to a first-round pick in the next draft and a second-round pick two years after that.

For the Jaguars, Monday’s trade will do little to keep them off the Super Bowl radar screen. Even without Bates and Davis, the Jaguars were a legitimate contender to make it to the Super Bowl. They will now become one of the favorites to win it all.

The Eagles have lost seven in a row. Trading Davis won’t do much to spark a turnaround. Some believed they had embarked on a soft tank. The tank has now gotten a little more concrete.

sports.title: Bills-Vikings game carries major significance for both teams
sports.summary: The Bills and Vikings have identical 0-4 records in the Super Bowl.
sports.body:
For Buffalo, which hopes to force the January road to SoFi Stadium through the open-air new venue in Western New York, it’s important to maintain distance between the 6-2 Jaguars and 7-2 Broncos. (The division is looking like the Bills’ to lose, with the Patriots now at 5-4.)

For Minnesota, their status as the last unbeaten team in the NFL could dissolve to being the last team out of the NFC playoff picture.

The NFC North, which now has a 20-3 record outside the division, has the Vikings at 6-1, the Bears at 7-2, the Lions are 6-2, and the Packers at 6-3. (Combined, they’ve lost as many games as the 0-8 Chargers.)

Last week, when the Vikings picked up their first loss of the season, the Lions, Bears, and Packers won. This week, the Lions, Bears, and Packers have won. A loss by the Vikings would conclude a two-week window in which the Vikings are 0-2, and the rest of the division is 6-0.

It gets worse. The 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams each won on Sunday. In the end, five playoff berths will go to the four teams of the NFC North and top three teams of the NFC West.

Two of those teams will be left out. And, frankly, the Vikings seem destined to be one of them.

Even with a 6-2 record, if they lose to the Bills. Because even though the defense is good enough to win a Super Bowl, the offense isn’t good enough to win a playoff game. It could be just bad enough to keep the team from making the playoffs.

It was one thing for the Vikings’ defense to not gripe when the end result of each game was victory. If the second game of a four-week gauntlet doesn’t go Minnesota’s way (the Packers and 49ers are up next), things could get even more awkward in the locker room.

sports.body: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. Payne also stands to benefit from the trade as he works his way back from a preseason injury that has kept him out of action so far this season.

sports.body: Over the last several weeks, we have seen the classic unraveling of a Jets season. The faces change, but the results always seem to stay the same. Entering Week 7, the Jets faced a two game homestand against beatable opponents. Victories against both the Dolphins and the Raiders would get the team to .500 through eight games and give this team real momentum heading into a tough stretch facing the Chiefs and Bills back-to-back. Of course, the Jets handed the previously winless Dolphins their first victory and then lost to the Raiders, dropping their record to 2-6. Not even at the halfway point, the season was over. It is normal for the competitive portion of the season to end early for Jets fans. It feels like an annual tradition in November to be discussing NFL Draft position above all else. The only thing the Jets still had going for them is it felt like the team was still united. Players were fighting for each other. Things changed in the Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets looked like an imploding team. Fans could see it in obvious ways like Minkah Fitzpatrick making a couple of business decisions when he had opportunities to make plays. Armand Membou threw his helmet in frustration in an emotional outburst after allow a second half sack. Geno Smith was demonstrative in his frustration frequently as the game slipped away. These are symptoms of a season that is slipping away and a team that is in a spiral. sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 - 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 - 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. sports.body: In the New York Jets’ ninth game of the 2026 season, on a gorgeous, warm and sunny day in Kansas City, Missouri, the Jets lost to the Kansas City Chiefs, 35 - 12. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They put together a nice drive, mixing runs and short passes effectively. Breece Hall and Braelon Allen combined to do much of the heavy lifting. The Jets got the ball down to the Chiefs five yard line before they were forced to settle for a chip shot field goal and an early 3 - 0 lead. The Jets defense then stepped up. They recovered a Justin Fields fumble on a quarterback sneak and the Jets quickly had the ball back in Chiefs territory. Unfortunately the Jets did not fully take advantage of the golden opportunity. They failed to get a first down and had to settle for another field goal. The Jets were up 6 - 0 late in the first quarter, but it felt like the points left on the field as they settled for field goals rather than touchdowns would come back to bite them later. The first quarter ended with the Chiefs knocking on the door, looking to go ahead with a first and goal at the Jets 7 yard line. sports.body: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Garrett Wilson Tim Patrick Blake Freeland Trevin Wallace Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Kohl Levao Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

sports.body: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. Today, for the first time this season, we’re handing out a pre-blame ball. It’s difficult to see a plausible Jets path to victory against the Chiefs in Kansas City, so pre-blame ball it is. Walker is second in the NFL with 110 rushing yards per game. He’s averaging a ridiculous 5.5 yards per carry. In short, Walker and the Kansas City running game are a problem for Chiefs opponents. A few weeks before that the Chicago Bears absolutely torched the Jets on the ground to the tune of 230+ rushing yards.
